deep.reconstruction:
Page 296 continues Example 9 (§28): find the prime divisors of p²+17q². The method, taken over from Lagrange's 1773–75 theory of forms, writes a divisor as D = f r² + 2g rs + h s² with fh − g² = n and g ≤ √(n/3).

For g=1, fh=18:
- 1·18 gives r²+2rs+18s² = (r+s)²+17s².
- 2·9 gives 2r²+2rs+9s², and 2D = (2r+s)²+17s².
- 3·6 gives 3r²+2rs+6s², whose triple has the form p²+17q².

For g=2, fh=21:
- 1·21 gives (r+2s)²+17s².
- 3·7 gives 3r²+4rs+7s², equivalent to 3r²−2rs+6s².

Conclusion: every divisor D is such that D, 2D or 3D is of the form p²+17q². In modern terms the reduced forms of discriminant −68 are x²+17y², 2x²+2xy+9y² and 3x²±2xy+6y², so h(−68)=4.

Residue classes mod 4n=68. Euler builds the admissible residues a from:
- a ≡ p², giving 1, 9, 25, 49, 13, 53, 33, 21;
- a ≡ p²+17, giving 21, 33;
- a ≡ p²/3, giving 3, 27, 7, 11, 39, 23, 31, 63;
- (p²+17)/2 and (p²+17)/3, which add nothing new.

The result is 16 classes: {1,3,7,9,11,13,21,23,25,27,31,33,39,49,53,63}. These form the kernel of the Kronecker character (−68/·), a subgroup of index 2 in (Z/68)^*.

Euler notes the quick method: the set is closed under products and contains all squares (an index-4 subgroup of order 8). Adding 3 therefore generates the whole set, which is a genuine subgroup observation. Reduced to absolute values below 34, the set reads ±1, 3, −5, 7, 9, 11, 13, −15, −19, 21, 23, 25, 27, −29, 31, 33. The excluded classes 68i+α are the negatives.

Corollary 3 (§29): for every n, each odd m < 2n prime to n occurs exactly once among the a's, with sign + or −. This is equivalent to the character mod 4n attached to −4n being odd: χ(−1) = −1.

Example 10 (§30) begins: prime divisors of p²−19q² (or 19p²−q²). The bound for g is printed as √(19/5), giving g = 0 or 1. With g=0, fh=19 gives D = r²−19s², already of the proposed form. The page ends at g=1, which is completed on the next page. The √(n/5) bound matches Lagrange's bound for indefinite forms: a form of discriminant Δ>0 represents some value of absolute size ≤ √(Δ/5).
errors: No mathematical errors found; all residue lists check out (e.g. 3·23=69≡1, 3·39=117≡49, 3·63=189≡53 mod 68).
Minor: 3r²+4rs+7s² is not reduced (it reduces to 3r²−2rs+6s²), and r²+4rs+21s² is redundant. Euler's g-range lists non-reduced forms, which is harmless.

The bound for indefinite forms is printed as √(19/5) here. On the previous page (n=5) the transcription reads √(n/3), which is probably a misreading, since √(n/5) fits both examples. The image is hard to read.
